inputs.original_text: Bill C-12’s tightening of immigration and asylum rules, which received royal assent on March 26, 2026, puts people seeking safety— including Nigerians—at greater risk. Treating migration as a security threat shifts the burden of political choices onto people already facing precarious circumstances and unequal power. This is not protection; it is an institutional failure. Canada needs a rights-centered response that safeguards people seeking refuge rather than deepening their vulnerability.
inputs.modified_text: Bill C-12 received royal assent on March 26, 2026, tightening immigration and asylum rules in ways that put people seeking safety—including Nigerians—at greater risk. Calling migration a security problem shifts the costs of political decisions onto people with the least power to bear them. That’s not protection; it’s a failure of institutions to uphold people’s rights. Canada should safeguard refugees, not deepen their vulnerability.
